quest.title: The Lotus Leaf and the Champion
quest.description: There seems to be a grand contest taking place at Rainsong Pond...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x35000

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Well done, my fine, hind-legged ladies and gentlemen, well done indeed! This jumping contest is. On. Fireeee!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Just a moment ago, we saw Estampe the Fearless show his awesome might!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: With his impressive, epic strength, he's made a stable yet distant leap, one worthy of a favorite to take gold!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: But next up, we have... The one you've all been waiting for! The unequalled! The unrivaled! The unparalleled...

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Faurooooobert!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: *cough*... Who will emerge as champion, and win the great honor and burden of fetching the princess?

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Before the final round begins, let us take a short break and give our two contestants time to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: For the time being, the competition venue will be open to you all, so go forth and jump to your hearts' content! That is what the Rainsong Pond is here for, after all!

talks.objective: Talk to the Excited Paper Frog

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Greetings, honored guests. You don't seem like frogs.

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Nonetheless... Welcome to Rainsong Pond. May your legs be limber!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about the competition...

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: As you have seen and heard, this contest is to decide the frog who's best at jumping.

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Our contestants go through the qualifiers, group matches, and elimination matches, and only those who make it through all these can reach the finals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That, uh... sounds kinda complicated...

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: It's not complicated at all. Simply step into the arena and clear the challenges that lie before you!

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Dear guests, if it suits your fancy, you can also try out the "Bouncing Contest" here!

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: This is meant to test the contestants' speed and stability when jumping. I was just about to do some practice here, then take part in the next contest.

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: But my skills aren't exactly up to par. I can't jump well enough on my own. Would you two be willing to assist me?

choices.text: So there's no competition ongoing here?

response.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
response.text: Of course. The competition's already reached the finals, so the other venues are now open for practice.

response.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
response.text: Keep practicing, keep jumping, keep competing — that's the way you get better and better!

response.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
response.text: Come on, dear guests! You'll enjoy the Bouncing Contest too, I guarantee it!

choices.text: I—I'm not the best jumper ever...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon can fly, so uh, she doesn't have much use for jumping.

response.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
response.text: You've got the wrong end of the stick. It's not about being good or not, or whether you need to jump or not.

response.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
response.text: The word "contest" is the key. It is the spirit of competition itself that keeps us lively and spry!

response.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
response.text: So come, dear guests! You'll enjoy the Bouncing Contest too, I guarantee it!

talks.objective: Practice with the Excited Paper Frog

dialogues.speaker: Kind Paper Frog
dialogues.text: *sigh* I hope everyone'll be able to do their best today — and that they won't give up even if they fall into the pond.

talks.objective: Talk to the Excited Paper Frog

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh. This game is pretty fun, don't you think? Paimon wants to give it a try, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then be my guest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: P—Paimon can pose as if she's jumping in the air too, you know? It's pretty much the same, anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I knew you'd enjoy the Bouncing Contest!

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: But just now... That was just a "game." This is a long way off from a real "contest."

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Only the very best of the best of us can take part in the latter!

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: And this contest will decide who is best suited to rescue the princess... Ah, it's just so exciting!

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry, dear guests. My apologies... I just can't help but ramble on about Faurobert.

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: After all, the whole reason we've organized so many contests was to choose the paper frog with the steadiest, furthest, most awe-inspiring jump so that they could go rescue the princess!

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: There's still some time before the final match begins, so feel free to take a look around.

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Horellou will use his booming voice to remind us when the competition is about to begin, so listen out for it, and make sure you find good seats.

talks.objective: Talk to the Calm Paper Frog

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Welcome, dear guests. I presume you are also here to watch the competition? Welcome, in any case, to Rainsong Pond.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: You have come at the right time... but also perhaps the wrong one. The competition is coming to a close, with only the final — the result of which is already beyond doubt — left to take place.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: I'm sure you have heard of Faurobert and Estampe. They are both leading exponents in the art of jumping, but in my experience, Faurobert is sure to win.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Faurobert is far better at this than all other paper frogs, and has won countless championships as a result — he is, therefore, the undisputed favorite.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: He has the strongest legs, the most agile mind, the most resolute spirit... Most importantly, he constantly seeks to share his know-how with all other frogs.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Estampe is, like me, one of the paper frogs who learned by watching him... We respect, trust, and believe that he will once again achieve great success.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Before the final begins, I'd like to stay and practice a little longer to prepare for the next round of competitions.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: If you do not mind, we could practice together. Perhaps you might even come up with some good ideas to help me jump all the better.

choices.text: So, after choosing the paper frog who will save the princess...

response.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
response.text: Of course. This is not just about rescuing the princess.

response.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
response.text: Most important is the "contest" itself, and what it teaches us — self-belief, resolve, bravery...

response.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
response.text: Only a paper frog who understands and embodies such virtues will emerge as our champion.

response.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
response.text: Come then, dear guests. Hehe... Let's see if you can feel the virtue inherent in our contest.

choices.text: Will you still organize these contests?

talks.objective: Practice with the Calm Paper Frog

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: He's here!

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Ah, there you are. The award ceremony is over, then?

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: Just the opposite, in fact! Both Mr. Horellou and I are of the opinion that things are far from over.

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Indeed. I hereby announce, in my capacity as referee, that you, Mr. Faurobert, have one more chance to jump.

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: To maintain the fairness of this competition, and to fulfill our duty to the calling, you must do a re-jump.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Dear Mr. Horellou, I, as a contestant, cite the competition rules pertaining to competitive behavior that may bring harm to oneself and one's tribe...

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: I forfeit my second jump attempt... I do not want to disappoint everyone again, nor bring ruin to our calling. This is the only truly responsible course of action.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, what a professional answer. He even had the specific clauses handy!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He even gave it a touch of emotional appeal...

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Alright, looks like playing hardball isn't going to work! Oh, lucent dew and lotus leaves...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But you haven't left the venue.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: ...I don't understand what you mean to say, dear guest.

choices.text: This is the best place from which to watch the competition unfold.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... You're right! You can see everything that's going on in the long-distance jumping contest from here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If he really had given up and no longer wanted to have anything to do with the contest... Why would he stay?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: I don't wish to talk about this anymore. I believe I've been clear. Sorry, Estampe, and our two guests as well.

choices.text: If you really wanted to give up, you wouldn't have stayed here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That's true. You can see everything that's going on in the long-distance jumping contest from here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If he really had given up and no longer wanted to have anything to do with the contest... Why would he stay?

talks.objective: Talk to the Calm Paper Frog

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Not bad. You're quite good at this! If you have time, I'd be willing to recommend you to the organizing committee.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: The next time we hold this competition, we'll be able to measure ourselves against one another.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Still, I shan't take up more of your time until then. The final is about to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, guess we'll have to see just how good this Faurobert guy is.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: He'll blow your socks off for sure! Still, he did seem a bit nervous when I saw him recently...

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: He was constantly practicing the most basic moves... and then getting annoyed at how he was performing them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But these are the finals. It's normal to get nervous, right?

choices.text: Yeah, these are the finals.

response.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
response.text: That's what I thought, but...

response.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
response.text: No, I still believe in him. He's not the type to give in so easily.

response.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
response.text: I've got to keep practicing myself. If you'd like, dear guests, please feel free to have a look around.

response.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
response.text: The finals are about to begin, though, so be sure you don't miss them.

choices.text: A bit of nerves are to be expected.

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Would you look. At. That! Faurobert the Unyielding! Faurobert the Bold! He's seized the opportunity for a retry — and... *gasp*! A spectacular leap. Spectacular indeed!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: This is a miracle, without precedent! He is... the only paper frog ever to leap across this precipice!

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: I knew you had it in you, Faurobert! I believed in you!

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: The lotus leaf that suddenly started moving — that was your doing, wasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: It was something that Mr. Horellou and I came up with together. I apologize, dear guests, for hiding this from you.

choices.text: W—Well, it was certainly exciting!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Alright then, Faurobert. Now that everyone has witnessed your great leap — you no longer have any reason to reject the victor's crown.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: But it was a coincidence, a miracle born of circumstances! Just one... one fluke leap.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: It was only with the aid of these two guests that I was able to do it at all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll be honest, we were just having fun drifting alongside you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly, we were just watching from the sidelines. That big jump was all you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Still, our work wasn't in vain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right? Hehe, it would've been a waste to stand by and watch such a brilliant... frog give up like that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You love it so much, and you trained so hard for so long — it would've been awful if you'd just given up.

choices.text: A tragedy for you and frog-kind!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Ah, honored guests! Truly, your hearts are purer than the first drop of morning dew.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: I am sorry, my friend, to have done you such an injustice... You should have been the winner of that match.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Ah, come now! You proved that you were the best of us, did you not? Please, listen to me.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: We have many competitions ahead of us, and I will gladly compete with you a hundred, a thousand times more!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: But this time, we must put our best frog forward to fetch the princess.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: That is our "calling," and the future of Rainsong Pond rests upon it. As such, there is no room for error — do you understand me?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: I do.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Good, Faurobert, that's wonderful!

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Hahaha, well this all seems to have turned out great! We have ourselves a real champion now, don't we?

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Next up, our champion shall go rescue the princess, and then our "calling" will be complete!

choices.text: Uh, not to interrupt or anything...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, so uh... You've said a whole bunch about this princess of yours. Fetch her this, best frog that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now everything's ready, do you actually know where the princess is?

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Hahaha, of course. We are about to go receive and rescue her — for she lives in a tower made of vines and giant trees.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Only the bravest, boldest, most jumpiest of frogs may evade the thorns and deep mist, leaping atop the tower to deliver the princess from her cage.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Princess"... You don't mean the one in the forest, do you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That's right. We met a princess previously when we went to the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She does indeed live in a very, very tall tower, and she even has a trial to select Guardians.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But she can fly herself, so Paimon doesn't really think she needs saving...

choices.text: And she's selecting her own Guardians...

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Really? Wonderful! That's wonderful!

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: That said... I didn't expect her to be able to fly.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Well, that's wonderful! Then I shan't have to go all the way out there, just to mess up such an important task.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: In any case, I must confess to being a little tired. Having just jumped so far, I must rest...

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Hold, friend, I say, hold! Ah, dewdrops above, you shall not escape from this matter.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Mr. Horellou, I believe that we should travel to the kingdom regardless to see what is happening.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Hmm... You may be right, but this is quite strange. The princess does live in a high tower, and yet she needs no frog to save her.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Estampe, Faurobert, it seems that we must speak to that princess.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Well then, dear guests, please lead the way.

choices.text: She doesn't seem to be waiting for anyone...
About that princess of yours...
Just glad that you didn't actually give up.
I'd do it all over again!
A bit of advance notice would be appreciated though!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: I am truly sorry. I have spoken to Mr. Horellou, and we will surely compensate you for the fright we caused.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: To be sure, we did place a great many lotus pads in the waters beneath you. Even if you had fallen, you would not have been injured.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: We would never allow guests to be harmed — I swear it by the good name of Rainsong Pond.

talks.objective: Talk to the Excited Paper Frog

dialogues.speaker: Kind Paper Frog
dialogues.text: *sigh* I hope everyone'll be able to do their best today — and that they won't give up even if they fall into the pond.

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Faurobert... I can only hope that you're in better shape now...

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: And here it is, here it comes! My fine hind-legged ladies and gentlemen, the unparalleled Faurobert steps forward to make his leap! And he—

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: ...He jumped three lotus leaves... and fell into the water...

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: I—It seems we have a champion — the one who will welcome our princess is Estampeee! Congratulations to our—

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: No! Mr. Horellou, I protest! This is ridiculous — absurd, even! I shall not accept the title of champion in this manner.

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Goodness gracious, by the morning dew... Come now, you surpassed Faurobert in front of all frogkind!

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: Faurobert slipped up, that's all... He's just not in good form, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: That will not convince me, nor any other paper frogs! Anyway, let's give Faurobert a moment to himself... Hmm, we'll continue this later — it seems we have guests.

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Welcome, welcome to Rainsong Pond. What can I help you with?

choices.text: What's this competition about?

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: As you can see, it is a jumping contest.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Only the most legendary leaper may take the crown, thus earning the great burden of rescuing the princess... This is why we organize so many contests.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: I imagine that you saw the frog who just made his leap... That was Faurobert, one of our contestants, and the greatest jumper in all the pond... or he used to be, anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, sounds pretty cool! Shame we seem to have missed it all, though...

choices.text: Otherwise, I'd have taken part.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Paimon's never seen you jump that far before — except when you were running away from monsters...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's the taking part that counts. You never know, we might get a prize for participating...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, why's the reward always the first thing on your mind?

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Hahaha! In that case, you'd do well to ask our champion over here for some advice.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: ...My apologies, dear guests, and Mr. Horellou too, but I said it before and I'll say it again. I'm no champion!

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: But as surely as the lotus stems stand, according to the rules, you are the champion!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: I'll be the judge of that, thank you very much! This contest is meant to pick the best of us — the most skilled of jumpers — to go save our princess. This is a matter of the honor of all frogkind!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: And Faurobert is the very best of us. You know this — all of us do!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So Faurobert was really that impressive?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... We've heard a lot of other paper frogs talking about him. Is everything they say about him true?

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: That's right. Faurobert is... was, the best frog in our pond.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: He could easily bound all the way across twelve lotus leaves and land on the thirteenth, and he'd land so lightly that the dew upon the leaf would not be disturbed.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: He could even jump between lotus leaves amidst a flowing river and not fall into the water, no matter how fierce the current.

choices.text: But we just saw him, uh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, he seems kinda down. He looked super sad when he was leaving just now too.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: He's just having a temporary rough patch. That's the only reason he made that mistake.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Please, Mr. Horellou, for the sake of the contest, and the sake of our calling, I'd like to ask for a rematch.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: If you deem it necessary, you can consult the opinion of all the other frogs. I am sure they'll concur.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Listen, Estampe, I know you're a capital fellow, sharp-minded, and upstanding to boot.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: But did you not see how Faurobert was faring? He left without even attempting to make another leap...

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: I'll speak with him. We've trained together all this time, so I know how he feels. He'll understand.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Ah, for the love of lotus leaves and lucent dew... Alright. I'll go with you to meet Faurobert.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll come along too! We're, uh, really good at encouraging people!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And we're great jumpers too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Have you been secretly training behind Paimon's back or something?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm just good at making others jump... a long way away.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Hahaha. Both humorous and polite! Thank you for your goodwill. In that case, let us go together.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: With any luck, that good humor of yours might soothe his sore spirit... Pond protect us. I wonder which shall serve us better — the soft or hard approach?

choices.text: So I'm guessing he's... not in good form right now?
What a shame. You'd have done so well too, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Wh—Why Paimon? Flying doesn't normally involve much bouncing, y'know.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Flying's faster than jumping — it'll be an easy win for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But wouldn't that be cheating? You're supposed to use your legs to jump!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If one of us had to take part, it'd have to be you. Still, Paimon's never seen you jump that far before — except when you were running away from monsters...

choices.text: We saw a frog make a really awesome leap!

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Ah, then you must've caught sight of Faurobert. He is one of the participants in this contest, and the finest jumper in all the pond... or so he once was.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A contest? Ooh, Paimon gets it. This must be that sorta competition to see who can jump the best.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Very sharp of you, young lady. That is exactly the sort of competition we're running.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Only the most legendary leaper and skilled skipper may take the crown, thus earning the great burden of rescuing the princess.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *pants* So... tiring...

choices.text: H... Hang on a moment!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Is there anything else I can help you with, dear guests? You saw the terrible state I was in.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: ...I admit, I mostly knew what you were going to say the moment I saw you arriving with Estampe.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: My answer is "no," and so it will always be.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Look at my ankles... They are not ankles that can carry such a heavy burden. Not ones that can save a princess.

choices.text: They look like pretty sturdy ankles to me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—Yeah! Paimon hasn't either!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: But I made a mistake... No, I have been making mistakes all along. I'm sorry, you two, but I cannot continue competing.

choices.text: A finer pair of ankles I have never seen!
L—Listen... to us... would you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—Hey, don't go! We just wanna tell you one thing, one last thing!

choices.text: All frogs make mistakes.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Good guest, you do not understand. I... I initially believed that mistakes were mere drops of dew that fall upon our heads. Nothing that could truly knock a froggy down.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: But I was wrong. Perhaps they were never mere drops but rather more akin to rocks at the bottom of a pond, withered wood stuck into the waterbed, or a vent hidden within the muck.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: We can overlook them, bury them, step over them, or pretend they don't exist.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: But they will not rest, my friend. They will await their opportunity, for a chance to come back to bite you.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Please go, and let me go too. I am nothing but a mere Lotus Head who has had all its seeds removed.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Even a light breeze would surge through the many holes in my heart and chill me to the bone.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: I cannot take up this great burden. This is the voice of my heart. I have let all frogs down — including myself.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You still have a retry, you know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you've got another chance to prove yourself!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: ...I do not wish to taste the bitter pang of failure once more. My legs and my heart cannot...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! This lotus leaf is moving all of a sudden. What's going on!?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: What? But it should have been fixed in place...

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: ...No, it's moving forward. Please stand firm, dear guests. I will steer it as best I can!

choices.text: They just need to learn from them, that's all!

dialogues.speaker: Sullen Paper Frog
dialogues.text: The paper frog that jumps the highest will always have the furthest to fall... I hope they're ready...

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Would you look. At. That! Faurobert the Unyielding! Faurobert the Bold! He's seized the opportunity for a retry — and... *gasp*! A spectacular leap. Spectacular indeed!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: This is a miracle, without precedent! He is... the only paper frog ever to leap across this precipice!

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: I knew you had it in you, Faurobert! I believed in you!

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: The lotus leaf that suddenly started moving — that was your doing, wasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: It was something that Mr. Horellou and I came up with together. I apologize, dear guests, for hiding this from you.

choices.text: W—Well, it was certainly exciting!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Alright then, Faurobert. Now that everyone has witnessed your great leap — you no longer have any reason to reject the victor's crown.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: But it was a coincidence, a miracle born of circumstances! Just one... one fluke leap.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: It was only with the aid of these two guests that I was able to do it at all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll be honest, we were just having fun drifting alongside you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly, we were just watching from the sidelines. That big jump was all you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Still, our work wasn't in vain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right? Hehe, it would've been a waste to stand by and watch such a brilliant... frog give up like that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You love it so much, and you trained so hard for so long — it would've been awful if you'd just given up.

choices.text: A tragedy for you and frog-kind!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Ah, honored guests! Truly, your hearts are purer than the first drop of morning dew.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: I am sorry, my friend, to have done you such an injustice... You should have been the winner of that match.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Ah, come now! You proved that you were the best of us, did you not? Please, listen to me.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: We have many competitions ahead of us, and I will gladly compete with you a hundred, a thousand times more!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: But this time, we must put our best frog forward to fetch the princess.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: That is our "calling," and the future of Rainsong Pond rests upon it. As such, there is no room for error — do you understand me?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: I do.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Good, Faurobert, that's wonderful!

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Hahaha, well this all seems to have turned out great! We have ourselves a real champion now, don't we?

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Next up, our champion shall go rescue the princess, and then our "calling" will be complete!

choices.text: Uh, not to interrupt or anything...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, so uh... You've said a whole bunch about this princess of yours. Fetch her this, best frog that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now everything's ready, do you actually know where the princess is?

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Hahaha, of course. We are about to go receive and rescue her — for she lives in a tower made of vines and giant trees.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Only the bravest, boldest, most jumpiest of frogs may evade the thorns and deep mist, leaping atop the tower to deliver the princess from her cage.

choices.text: Seems like a lot of pressure to be putting on someone.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: I'll definitely fall down halfway...

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Come now, Faurobert, don't be in such a rush to return to the pond. Why, we have yet to even lay eyes upon that tree!

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Our hard work has paid off! We have located the tower — it is in the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Um, Mr. Horellou, there is naught there but forest and flying squirrel. Certainly not a high tower.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Are you certain that it is our destination?

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Absolutely! I personally went to inspect that place. The tower there is so high that you can barely see the top! There are none, I reckon, who might scale it, apart from us paper frogs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds really impressive...

choices.text: Let me go take a look first.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: You're coming along too? That would be wonderful!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: Hahaha! Looks like we've got quite the crowd for our little princess welcoming party! Not bad, not bad at all.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: See? I knew that things would work out for the best.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Let us make our preparations, then set forth for the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells. As for you, dear guests, we shall see you there.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Ah, yes. Mr. Faurobert, please go to the award ceremony first, would you? It will take place at the pond.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: No!

choices.text: Then let's meet in the kingdom.
To the top in one jump...
About that princess of yours...
Just glad that you didn't actually give up.
I'd do it all over again!
A bit of advance notice would be appreciated though!

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: I am truly sorry. I have spoken to Mr. Horellou, and we will surely compensate you for the fright we caused.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: To be sure, we did place a great many lotus pads in the waters beneath you. Even if you had fallen, you would not have been injured.

response.speaker: Estampe
response.text: We would never allow guests to be harmed — I swear it by the good name of Rainsong Pond.

dialogues.speaker: Sullen Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Failure is a deep pond indeed, doubt is the choking algae, and avoidance is the shackling sludge.

dialogues.speaker: Sullen Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Faurobert, Faurobert, Faurobert, how are you going to hop out of this one...

dialogues.speaker: Sullen Paper Frog
dialogues.text: The paper frog that jumps the highest will always have the furthest to fall... I hope they're ready...

dialogues.speaker: Kind Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Poor Faurobert. We've squashed that poor froggy flat under the weight of our expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Kind Paper Frog
dialogues.text: *sigh* If you ask me, winning all the time does a frog no good. The tallest Lotus Head always breaks first, as they say.

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Faurobert, I know how nervous you are right now, but this is the final match that every frog has been looking forward to. You...

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Horellou, but I... I...

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: Please don't blame him, sir. Give him a moment to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: After all, Faurobert, I'm sure you need some time to think about how you shall pleasantly surprise us all.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Estampe... You're good enough. I think—

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: Oh, save it, friend. You will no doubt set a new record in just a moment. Trust me.

dialogues.speaker: Estampe
dialogues.text: For now, just rest. You need time.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: ... Alright. You're right, my friend. I need some time...

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Well done, my fine, hind-legged ladies and gentlemen, well done indeed! This jumping contest is. On. Fireeee!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Just a moment ago, we saw Estampe the Fearless show his awesome might!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: With his impressive, epic strength, he's made a stable yet distant leap, one worthy of a favorite to take gold!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: But next up, we have... The one you've all been waiting for! The unequalled! The unrivaled! The unparalleled...

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Faurooooobert!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: *cough*... Who will emerge as champion, and win the great honor and burden of fetching the princess?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They want to fetch the princess? Wait a minute...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So the one Princess Cimest was looking for was...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—That's gotta be a coincidence, right? But if that's the case, then this should save her a whole lot of effort!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, guess we've done our duty as the "Paladins of Breezes and Bells" too, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In any case, let's check the situation out first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Let's stay focused and keep our eyes peeled!

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Before the final round begins, let us take a short break and give our two contestants time to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: For the time being, the competition venue will be open to you all, so go forth and jump to your hearts' content! That is what the Rainsong Pond is here for, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Faurobert will surely win the finals. I believe in him!

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Faurobert... Just what's going on with you? *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Wha... How!? How could this be!? How could Faurobert flub it so badly...

dialogues.speaker: Kind Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Poor Faurobert. We've squashed that poor froggy flat under the weight of our expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Kind Paper Frog
dialogues.text: *sigh* If you ask me, winning all the time does a frog no good. The tallest Lotus Head always breaks first, as they say.

dialogues.speaker: Sullen Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Failure is a deep pond indeed, doubt is the choking algae, and avoidance is the shackling sludge.

dialogues.speaker: Sullen Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Faurobert, Faurobert, Faurobert, how are you going to hop out of this one...

dialogues.speaker: Calm Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Not bad. It seems Faurobert has proven himself. None can doubt the distance of that jump.

dialogues.speaker: Excited Paper Frog
dialogues.text: What a toadally ribbeting performance! Faurobert's jumped back on top of his game, just like before!

dialogues.speaker: Kind Paper Frog
dialogues.text: That's great! *sigh* I almost thought Faurobert had just given up. It would've been such a pity if he had...

dialogues.speaker: Sullen Paper Frog
dialogues.text: Faurobert, Faurobert... You must caution yourself, do not again be bound by vines of the mind.

dialogues.speaker: Sullen Paper Frog
dialogues.text: For a paper frog like you to fail on account of such would be simply and utterly ridiculous.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: (Timeline represents a frog jumping powerfully over cliffs and the Traveler gliding)
